extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — scientists, engineers, and educated public
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used in short reviews and reports for judging scientific books, papers, museums, lectures, and research summaries — emphasizing clarity, illustration, practicality, referencing, and suitability for intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum usefulness for engineers
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical museum should have departmental organization (railway, naval, civil engineering), explanatory notes on many exhibits, cross-sections to illustrate internal arrangement, some models operable by visitors (with notification), occasional demonstrations of particularly interesting plant models by officials, and supporting materials such as diagrams, photographs, statistical tables, a reading room and a library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features together make the institution of real service to engineers; interactive exhibits, clear explanatory material, and supporting documentation are emphasized as practical necessities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and financing of extension lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension lectures should bring scientific knowledge in a popular form to societies unable to pay large fees; lecturing and demonstrating are voluntary and gratuitous for lecturers, but charges are made for hire of slides, travelling and out-of-pocket expenses; fees are also charged for commercial or government-subsidised societies, and all fees paid are devoted to the working expenses of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies intended audience (societies with limited funds) and acceptable cost-recovery practice; distinguishes when additional fees are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and purpose-fit of geological illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Geological papers should be accompanied by clearly labelled sections and an admirable series of sections often showing rival readings and gathered from various authors; sections should show stages of growth which lead to the geological interpretation (e.g., system of overfolds); reproducing panoramas and well-drawn diagrams aids the paper's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good labelling, comparative sections and sequence-of-growth illustrations make a geological paper 'perfect for its purpose'; absence of such clarity reduces usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical design of field guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Field guides intended for use in all weathers should avoid awkward design choices (e.g., transparent sheets with printed rock-layer names used as indexes may be impractical in the field); illustrations should be neat and robust for outdoor use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate portability, durability, and ease-of-use in field conditions in addition to informational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, accurate popular scientific accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Works summarising large-scale research for broader audiences should be well written, illustrated by good charts and plates, demand no great previous knowledge of the reader, yet be accurate — serving to educate public opinion on the utility of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance readability and technical accuracy; effective use of illustrations and clear exposition are key to public value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate citation of prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific papers should cite previous workers and literature adequately; absence of references (or scant reference) renders diagrams and arguments of little help and makes it uncertain how the author links with predecessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References provide context and allow readers to assess novelty and relation to earlier theories; missing references are a substantive shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of experimental reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental studies should present a full account of the experimental work together with a review of relevant literature (e.g., Osborne's wheat-protein work combines full experimental detail with a brief literature review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive methods and experimental detail permit assessment and replication; include concise literature synthesis to situate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of genetic characters (consider compound characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: When experimental crosses give apparently anomalous results, authors should consider that what appears as a single distinguishing character may be compound (multiple underlying characters) rather than a single allelomorph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genetic explanations should allow for multilocus or composite-character models (as Cuenot/Shull discussion illustrates) rather than forcing single-factor interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic nomenclature correctness and conservatism
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should maintain grammatically correct, well-known scientific names (e.g., retain 'Lepidosteus' rather than changing to an alternative rendering), even if an alternative might be the original rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for grammatical correctness and established usage in taxonomic names is important to avoid unnecessary confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation prudence and enforceability in policy advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy recommendations (e.g., fisheries management proposals) should be founded on fully sifted evidence and should consider practicability and enforceability; premature restrictive legislation is ill-advised before the International Council has thoroughly examined evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should avoid overstepping evidence; when proposing regulation, explicitly discuss means of enforcement and practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific measurable regulatory proposals (with implementation caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: When recommending regulatory measures, provide specific, measurable limits (e.g., inshore size limits for plaice, a minimum landing length for offshore-caught fish) while acknowledging the complexity and challenges of enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete numeric recommendations are useful but should be accompanied by discussion of how they could be practically enforced and gradually implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation and cooperation in observational science
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative international work (e.g., hydrography) benefits from standardisation of instruments and methods; such cooperation improves the quality and comparability of data across nations and regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise methodological standardisation and shared protocols in multi-national observational programmes to make results comparable and actionable.
